headline: Remulla Calls for Stronger Gun-Owner Liability After Zamboanga School Shooting
seoTitle: Remulla Calls for Stronger Gun-Owner Liability After Zamboanga Shooting | FMB News
seoDescription: Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla urged stronger penalties for negligent gun owners after the Ateneo de Zamboanga school shooting, as investigators continue examining how the student accessed his father's firearms.
deck: The fatal school shooting has renewed scrutiny of firearm safekeeping and whether Philippine law should impose stronger criminal liability when licensed weapons are accessed by minors.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: A shooting at a school attached to Ateneo de Zamboanga University in Zamboanga City on August 18 left two students dead, including the suspected shooter, and two other people injured. Authorities continue to investigate how the student obtained firearms belonging to his father, a Bureau of Customs official.

Reuters reported on August 19 that Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla urged lawmakers to stiffen penalties for gun owners whose firearms are accessed by minors and to revisit laws governing loose firearms. FMB News is not treating the email package's separate claim about mandatory biometric firearm storage as verified because that specific proposal was not independently corroborated.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Republic Act No. 10591 already requires licensed firearm owners to keep firearms in a vault, locked container or under other security measures. The law also provides for safekeeping with the PNP Firearms and Explosives Office or police regional offices.

Remulla had also called for stronger criminal accountability for negligent firearm owners after the June 2026 Tacloban school shooting, arguing that existing rules do not clearly impose criminal liability on every licensed owner when another person uses the registered firearm in a crime. The Zamboanga shooting has renewed that policy debate.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The case raises two separate questions: how the firearms were physically accessed in this specific investigation, and whether existing Philippine firearms law provides sufficient accountability when a licensed weapon is negligently stored and later used by a minor. Those questions should remain distinct until investigators and lawmakers establish the relevant facts and any proposed statutory changes.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for formal PNP and Bureau of Customs findings on firearm access and chain of custody, any administrative or criminal proceedings, and any bill or officially released amendment proposal that would change the liability or storage requirements under Republic Act No. 10591.
